title: A metric with no local isometric immersion
description: Tools for isometric immersions of surfaces in three-dimensional space: the height equation, a metric with a given small curvature, and the boundary of a disk of negative curvature. The second lesson constructs a smooth metric on a square and proves OpenAI's theorem (2026) that no neighbourhood of the centre has a smooth isometric immersion into three-dimensional space, from one named statement on the height equation, the patch obstruction, which the course does not prove. The third lesson derives the linear equation satisfied by high derivatives of a solution of the height equation, the starting point of the proof of that statement.
prerequisites: the lesson Submanifolds and hypersurfaces (course Bundles, curvature and holonomy), Proposition A.3: the Gauss formula in coordinates and the Gaussian curvature as det II / det g
core course Real Analysis: differentiation under the integral, uniform convergence of series of derivatives, the inverse function theorem
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the patch obstruction (P), which is a named hypothesis of the second lesson
